column4: This event failed on top of deposits from the 2016 Lamplugh Glacier event (EID 81).

This event registered on the LDEO Surface Wave Event Locations website (Ekström 2022)a. The entry time was 2022-09-17 18:10:24 (UTC) at a location of 58.75, -136.75 with a surface wave magnitude of 5.2.
Centerline, total area, and source areas were digitized using PlanetScope satellite imagery. L and H were estimated using the centerline and crown and toe locations.

This event was seismically detected by Matt Haney at the Alaska Volcano Observatory (Petley, 2022c). Additional satellite images of the event can be seen at https://blogs.agu.org/landslideblog/2022/09/23/lamplugh-glacier-1/.
A photograph and visualization of the event are available in this thread: https://twitter.com/WaterSHEDLab/status/1572202447032188928 (Dan Shugar, 2022).

Volume estimates determined by bedrock landslide values in Larsen and others (2010) with bedrock scar geometry. Volume_high and Volume_low estimates made by propagating uncertainties in alpha and gamma values (Larsen and others, 2010) and standard deviation of source areas (Area_Source_high, Area_source_low, Area_source). Estimates rounded to two significant digits.

Raw waveforms from closest stations. Data was demeaned but no other processing was applied. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present.

High frequency (1-5 Hz) ground velocity waveforms from closest stations with detections. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Waveforms are corrected for station response after removing the mean. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Clipped waveforms have not been removed before station correction so check raw plots before interpreting high amplitude signals.

Long period (20-60 sec) ground displacement waveforms from closest stations with detections. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database, based on high frequency waveform). Waveforms are corrected for station response after detrending using a linear fit and tapering. Zero mean cosine filter applied with station correction may cause acausal arrivals. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Signals with clipped waveforms and data gaps have not been removed so check raw figures before interpreting.

Displacement spectrum from closest broadband stations with detections, corrected for station response with no prefiltering after detrending using a linear fit and tapering. Note that long period signals often contain noise unrelated to the event signal of interest, especially on horizontal components (e.g. tilt), so interpret with care. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Signals with clipped waveforms and data gaps have not been removed so check raw figures before interpreting.
Spectrograms of velocity waveforms corrected for station sensitivity from closest stations with detections. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present

Multitaper spectra (same units as Power Spectral Density) of velocity waveforms corrected for station sensitivity from closest stations with detections. Linear trend was removed and a taper was applied before generating spectra. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Since station response was not removed to avoid adding artifacts at low frequencies for short and intermediate period stations, the lower frequency amplitudes should be interpreted with care.

Raw infrasound waveforms from closest stations. Data was demeaned but no other processing was applied. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present.

Filtered infrasound (0.5-2 Hz) waveforms for station response from closest stations with detections. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Waveforms are corrected for station response after removing the mean. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present.
